stories.headline: How the Atlanta Dream turned their franchise around in just five years
stories.summary: Five years ago, the Dream were the second-worst team in the WNBA -- making their Finals run all the more remarkable.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Just five years ago, the idea of the Atlanta Dream competing for the WNBA championship trophy would have seemed as unlikely as a rebound landing untouched next to Angel Reese.

So finishing within one victory of a title, as the Dream did in the WNBA Finals last week, says a lot about just how far the franchise has come since 2021. Even without the 2026 championship, what the Dream did in revitalizing their franchise is a story that shouldn't be lost in Golden State's celebration. Five years ago, the Dream were a mess. Now, they're contenders. That's something other WNBA franchises can look to.

"It's remarkable, really," Atlanta coach Karl Smesko said.

Consider how far the franchise was from this in 2021.

That was the year the Dream moved to Gateway Center Arena -- the smallest venue in the WNBA at 3,500 seats -- because too much of their longtime larger home (State Farm Arena, capacity 17,608) was vacant during games. The Dream had three different coaches that year, one resigning just before the season began to take a college job. Chennedy Carter, their lottery-pick selection from 2020, was suspended in July and never returned. They finished in second-to-last place in the WNBA at 8-24.

The team's most notable moment came not on court, but in a viral video of two Dream players throwing punches by a food truck outside an Atlanta nightclub.

Those were the low points. But behind the scenes, two big moves in 2021 helped spark a turnaround: an ownership change, led by real estate investor Larry Gottesdiener, and a new general manager, Dan Padover.

Reese was then a college sophomore with huge goals for her future. But it wasn't until this April that she knew those plans would intersect with the Dream.

"When I play with joy and I'm surrounded by people that just genuinely make me happy, I think I'm at my best," Reese said. "The organization has poured into me. To be in my third year [in the WNBA], this is obviously the best situation I've ever been in."

And even as Reese and teammates Jordin Canada and Allisha Gray sat somberly in the Dream's postgame news conference after Game 7, the joyful sounds of Ballhalla's celebration audible, they looked dissatisfied but not devastated.

"They changed my life," Reese said of the Atlanta players and staff. "And I'm just so grateful for them."

A 2008 EXPANSION TEAM, the Dream's first title hopes were led by another Angel -- 2009 No. 1 pick Angel McCoughtry. She led the Dream to the Finals in 2010, 2011 and 2013, but they were swept each time.

The Dream then missed the playoffs six of the next nine years. They won a then-franchise record 23 games in 2018, but lost McCoughtry to a knee injury Aug. 7 and lost 3-2 in the semifinals.

Without McCoughtry in 2019, the Dream averaged just 4,270 fans for home games, necessitating the move from State Farm Arena. That relocation was delayed a year because of the COVID-19 pandemic, when the 2020 season was in a "bubble" in Bradenton, Florida. By then, McCoughtry had left in free agency for Las Vegas.

The Dream's leadership became a focus for all WNBA players in the bubble when co-owner Kelly Loeffler sent a letter to commissioner Cathy Engelbert opposing the league's decision to display "Black Lives Matter" logos on the courts in Bradenton. Loeffler wrote "we need less -- not more -- politics in sports."

Loeffler was involved in a political race at the time, seeking to hold her U.S. Senate seat. The divide mushroomed into WNBA players campaigning for her opponent, Raphael Warnock.

"Being on the outside of the Dream looking in then, during that time everybody was rallying around them," said guard Jordin Canada, then with the Seattle Storm, of the bubble activism against Loeffler's continued ownership. "We wanted what was best for them and the W as a whole, and to see that transition into a more positive direction."

The situation was untenable, and the franchise was sold in February 2021 to Gottesdiener's group, which included former WNBA player Renee Montgomery.

"I believed the WNBA was an extraordinary opportunity, not just to grow the game of basketball," Gottesdiener said, "but to demonstrate what's possible when you invest in women."

Padover, who joined the Dream in October 2021, had worked for the Las Vegas Aces for three years, helping build the team that would become a three-time champion. He went from a franchise a step from the top to one with nowhere to go but up.

Padover started his WNBA career as a video coordinator with the New York Liberty in 2012, and he has credited former coach and GM Bill Laimbeer for helping him develop into a team executive. He cites this key from Laimbeer.

"If you can get your organization organized and you can take care of the players, you can start to establish yourself as a place that is respected," Padover said. "Under previous ownership, I think we were disorganized, and we didn't really have an identity.

"When I got here the goal was, 'Let's turn Atlanta back into a franchise that's respected throughout the WNBA community, one piece at a time, and that will allow us to be able to build something.' We started with things like player housing, staffing, and medical and player development."

THE OTHER PIECE was putting the right players and coaches in the building. Padover, who has been named the league's executive of the year three times, put his trade wizardry to use. He dealt the Nos. 3 and 14 picks in the 2022 draft and a 2023 pick swap to Washington for the No. 1 pick in 2022 to select Rhyne Howard.

"It was a huge boost of confidence," Howard said. "Obviously, when you get drafted, that means the team wants you. But to do it in the way that they did -- trading up to get me like that -- put no doubt in my mind that I was a piece that they were looking for to start this new journey, to start this new outcome that we're having."

The 6-foot-2 guard was Rookie of the Year and has since been a four-time All-Star. She averaged 17.7 points in the regular season this year and 16.3 in the playoffs. Howard won't recall Game 7 fondly -- she was limited to six points on 3-of-14 shooting -- but she took noticeable steps forward as a player in 2026, especially on defense.

Padover also got the steal of the second round in 2022 with forward Naz Hillmon, who became a full-time starter this season and has played more WNBA games than anyone from that draft class.

Subsequent huge deals came for guards Gray (2023) and Canada (2024).

"One of the things that I definitely took from Bill was not to be skittish to give up things in trades," Padover said. "If you're doing it to get a great player, it's always worth it, and don't be afraid to do that."

One of Padover's biggest moves in 2025 was bringing in Smesko, who had spent most of his career as a college coach, including 17 years at Florida Gulf Coast.

"Obviously, there was a changing landscape in college basketball, and I was at the point where a new challenge was needed," Smesko said of his decision to move to the WNBA. "It was Atlanta, and I love the city. And I thought there was the makings of a core that could compete for a championship."

Atlanta went 30-14 last season but lost in the first round of the playoffs. Padover used a trade to acquire the last key component. On April 6, the Dream obtained Reese from the Chicago Sky for future draft picks. Reese had become disillusioned with the Sky's direction and voiced her concerns near the end of the 2025 season. She believed in the Dream's vision, just as the players obtained before her did.

"I feel like the organization has gotten to a point where players want to come play for Atlanta," Gray said. "To be able to get Angel just speaks volumes of how the organization is run and how it really cares for players. The city of Atlanta is great. Great culture. The games just feel like one big family cookout, and everybody's welcome."

Reese proved to be the final and most essential ingredient. Other than a five-game skid June 24-July 4, the Dream -- who also added veteran DeWanna Bonner late in the season -- stayed consistent, finishing 30-14 again. Reese had the best offensive year of her career, averaging 16.4 points, plus 12.1 rebounds.

"She's made me look good all season long," Howard said. "And I'm sure she's going to continue to do that for the rest of her time here. Shoutout to her for coming in and being bought in. She's handled every challenge that we've thrown at her with grace."

This year's Finals games in Atlanta didn't come without hurdles -- facility conflicts with State Farm Arena meant one Finals game had to be moved up a day and another had to be played at 12:30 p.m. ET on a Thursday. But even that early game was joyful and loud, a full house of fans skipping work and school to cheer on the Dream in a must-win Game 6.

Next year, the Dream moves back to State Farm Arena full time, playing all 25 regular-season home games there.

And as disappointed as the Dream were after losing Game 7, they also immediately expressed excitement about the 2027 season.

"Just because we didn't win today doesn't mean that we won't be champions in the future," Reese said.

Those words weren't just platitudes after a disappointing ending. Next year, with every starter already signed to return, the Dream could at last win that elusive title.

"I like our chemistry and just the sisterhood that we have as a team," said Gray, who played every Finals game despite sustaining an injury on her shooting hand in the semifinals. "We actually love each other and enjoy being around each other."

stories.headline: Fantasy buzz: Wilson in protocol, Tuten GTD for TNF, four teams make QB changes
stories.summary: Two sure fantasy starters are unsure to play this week, while QB news was plentiful.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Nov. 4: Garrett Wilson's concussion could create more opportunities for Jets playmakers
By Eric Moody

New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn announced Wednesday that Wilson is in the concussion protocol. Wilson played the entire game against the Las Vegas Raiders last week, finishing with six catches for 83 yards on 12 targets. If cleared, I'd still start Wilson as a low-end WR2, even though the Chiefs have allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

If Wilson cannot play, Adonai Mitchell is the first receiver I'd look to add. Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown last week, finishing with 27.2 fantasy points. I'd view Mitchell as an upside WR4.

Omar Cooper Jr. could also see more targets, but I'd leave him on the bench. He had consecutive 100-yard games before going without a target against the Raiders.

Mason Taylor is worth considering if you need help at tight end. He's drawn at least five targets in three consecutive games and faces a Chiefs defense that has allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game to the position.

Have a plan in the event of a Jonathan Taylor trade
Jonathan Taylor has been mentioned in trade rumors, and there's a chance the Indianapolis Colts move him before Sunday. Managers who roster Taylor should add Seth McGowan (rostered in 21.6% of ESPN leagues) as insurance. If Taylor is traded (or made a Sunday inactive while the team continues to work on a deal), McGowan could see a much larger workload against a Cowboys defense that's allowed the sixth-most fantasy points per game to running backs.

Nov. 4: Bhayshul Tuten questionable for Thursday night
By Michael DiRocco, NFL Nation Jaguars reporter

Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) likely will be a game-time decision for Thursday night's game in Baltimore, coach Liam Coen said Wednesday. Tuten, who is coming off the best game of his career (104 yards, a TD and a TD catch), did not practice at all this week. Tuten leads the Jaguars in rushing (492 yards). If he's unable to play, the Jaguars will likely start Chris Rodriguez Jr and behind him will be Ameer Abdullah and LeQuint Allen Jr.

Nov. 4: Shedeur Sanders could start with Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol
By Eric Moody

Watson entered the concussion protocol Tuesday after reporting symptoms from a helmet-to-helmet hit in Sunday's loss to Pittsburgh. If he can't clear it in time for Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints, Sanders would likely start. He averaged just 11.9 fantasy points per game in seven starts last season, throwing seven touchdowns and nine interceptions. That's not encouraging for a Browns passing offense that ranks 22nd in passing yards per game this season.

Quinshon Judkins led the Browns' backfield with 13 touches against Pittsburgh but scored only 6.9 fantasy points, as Dylan Sampson led the backfield in snaps and routes, finishing with 12.9 fantasy points. The matchup against the Saints is much better for Judkins, as they allowed the most fantasy points per game to running backs. I'd still view him as a low end RB2, but his workload could be reduced if Cleveland falls behind again. Sampson is worth holding in most leagues and has flex appeal in deeper formats.

KC Concepcion was among Cleveland's leaders in routes against Pittsburgh but saw only four targets and scored 6.7 fantasy points. Harold Fannin Jr. (12 targets) and Denzel Boston (11) both saw more targets last week. I'd have a hard time trusting Concepcion or Boston in most fantasy lineups if Sanders starts..

Fannin is the one Cleveland pass catcher I'd feel comfortable starting. He caught 10 passes for 154 yards last week and has drawn at least nine targets in consecutive games. He's best viewed as a low-end TE1 if Sanders starts.

Nov. 4: Darnold out, Milton to start, Brissett traded
By Adam Rank

Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Sunday's game because of a quad injury he sustained on Monday night. Darnold has not been placed on IR, so you're going to need to either release him (which is fine in single-quarterback leagues) or put him on the bench in superflex leagues. The latter makes the most sense for Drew Lock as a replacement option.

However, if you're in traditional leagues with a realistic waiver wire, my first option would be to look at Malik Willis, who has averaged more than 20 points in Week 7 and 8. Willis has an advantageous matchup against the Detroit Lions, who have been very generous to opposing quarterbacks -- particularly mobile quarterbacks. The Lions are dead last against the pass (24.7 fantasy points per game).

Joe Milton was named the Philadelphia Eagles' starter, replacing Tanner McKee. Milton doesn't offer much upside for those of you in redraft leagues that start one QB. Don't even bother to make a waiver claim. However, if you're like me and you play in a superflex dynasty league, now we're talking. In fact, I'm in two such leagues. In one, I already had him rostered. In the other, I put in a huge claim for him. Mostly because my two starting quarterbacks are Jaxson Dart (IR) and Justin Herbert. And yes, I'm coming to the stunning realization Milton might be my best starting quarterback if I do end up getting him. I kid, but just barely.

The thing that intrigues me about Milton is his rushing ability. He had over 400 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns at Tennessee. And he's shown some flashes of mobility during very limited time as an NFL quarterback. I'm getting dangerously close to starting him in redraft, but will just opt for the dynasty play here.

In additional quarterback news, ESPN is reporting that QB Jacoby Brissett is expected to be traded to the Baltimore Ravens over the weekend. While Brissett is a streamable option moving forward, this is great news for Ravens WR Zay Flowers. There is concern about Flowers this Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but he will move back to his low-end WR1/WR2 status if the deal for Brissett is completed.

Nov. 3: Bears roster full of must-starts, Seahawks ease Charbonnet back into mix

By Michael F. Florio

The Chicago Bears offense continued rolling on the road Monday night against the defending Super Bowl champs. D'Andre Swift was the star of the show, turning 30 opportunities into 79 yards and three touchdowns. He finished with 27.9 fantasy points and surely dragged many fantasy teams from the jaws of defeat.

Luther Burden III stayed hot, racking up seven catches on nine targets for 56 yards and a touchdown. He finished with 18.6 fantasy points and has averaged 19.9 fantasy points per game since Caleb Williams returned in Week 6. He has emerged as the Bears' top pass catcher and is a weekly start.

Tight end Colston Loveland also saw nine targets, catching seven for 65 yards (and losing a fumble) to finish with 11.5 fantasy points. He has averaged 16.6 fantasy points per game since Williams returned. He should be started each week.

More takeaways from Monday

Williams played extremely well, even if it did not translate to the biggest fantasy game. He is the first QB to throw for over 200 yards against the Seattle Seahawks defense this season. He finished with 13.98 fantasy points. That is more about the matchup though. Williams should be started weekly.
Rome Odunze saw six targets, catching four for 87 yards, good for 12.7 fantasy points, his second-highest mark in a game this season. It's great to see Odunze produce, but he remains the third target in this Bears passing game. That makes him a low-floor, high-upside flex option.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba continues to be the Seahawks' offense. He saw 11 targets, catching six for 118 yards and a touchdown. He deserves to be in the MVP conversation and should be viewed as the best WR in fantasy football. He has one game with less than 22.8 fantasy points this season (12.6 in Week 4). He has 52% of his team's receiving yards. No other player even has 40%.
Both Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet returned from injury in Week 9. Price led the way, playing 48% of snaps and logging 10 carries and four targets. He finished with 37 total yards and 5.7 fantasy points. Charbonnet played 36% of snap and saw six carries and four targets. He went for 29 yards and finished with 5.9 fantasy points. The Seahawks have a better matchup next week against the Arizona Cardinals, but splitting the usage leaves both running backs purely as flex options.
Sam Darnold continued to struggle, but he ended up having a solid fantasy night, as Seattle was trailing and having to throw. He finished with 188 passing yards, two touchdowns, one interception and 17.52 fantasy points. Darnold has nine interceptions in his last six games. Still, he is a streaming option next week against the Cardinals, who are tied for the most passing touchdowns allowed in the league (18).

Nov. 2: How the move to Minshew impacts the Cardinals

By Michael F. Florio

The Arizona Cardinals named Gardner Minshew II as their starting quarterback on Monday for the Week 9 game in Seattle against the Seahawks.

Minshew took over for Jacoby Brissett on Sunday against Dallas and threw for 188 yards and three touchdowns in a comeback win against the Cowboys, but faces a much tougher task next week against Seattle.

The biggest question is what this means for the Cardinals' pass catchers, but here's how I expect the switch at QB to impact all positions on offense.

While a QB change always adds some volatility, Trey McBride remains a must-start tight end. McBride is a must start regardless of who the QB is, but Minshew's tendency to target tight ends at a high rate keeps him as an elite option. In both 2023 and 2024, Minshew threw to tight ends 12% of the time, which is actually a higher rate than Brissett this season (10%).
Due to volume, Michael Wilson will remain in play in most matchups. However, next week against Seattle is a week to get him out of your starting lineup. The Cardinals next three weeks are tough matchups for Wilson. Outside of Wilson, fantasy managers should avoid the rest of the Cardinals receivers for the time being.
The running backs could see a bump in targets as well, as Minshew has always targeted running backs at a high rate. His career average is 17%, while Brissett is at 13% this season.
As for Minshew himself, fantasy managers should stay away with the next three weeks being the Seahawks, Rams and Chiefs. For Week 9, some more favorable streaming options are Kyler Murray (or potentially Carson Wentz), Malik Willis, Sam Darnold and C.J. Stroud.

It is worth noting that since 2021, there have been 12 relief performances of 15 or more fantasy points by quarterbacks who went on to make another start at some point in that given season; that group averaged 6.7 fewer fantasy points as starters (shout out to Tristan H. Cockcroft for the stat!).

Nov. 2: Notebook for Week 8

By Eric Moody

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills

Derrick Henry's playing time has declined over the past two weeks, falling below 50% of snaps against the Bills. On Sunday, he rushed for 53 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, marking his third straight game with fewer than 60 rushing yards. Justice Hill played on more snaps and ran more routes compared to Henry's nine, benefiting from Baltimore playing from behind. With Lamar Jackson headed for IR due to a thumb injury, the Ravens could struggle to sustain drives and generate red zone opportunities, making Henry's fantasy outlook even more concerning going forward.
Dalton Kincaid played through a chest injury against the Ravens and delivered his second-best fantasy performance (18.6 fantasy points) of the season, catching four out of six targets for 86 yards and a touchdown. Kincaid continues to share playing time with Dawson Knox, but his involvement in the passing game remains encouraging. He ran 23 routes (compared to Knox's 17) and his targets per route remain high despite a slight decline in snaps. Kincaid has now stockpiled 14 targets over his past two games and remains a solid TE1 heading into Week 9 against the Vikings.

Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals

Wan'Dale Robinson continues to be Tennessee's most reliable receiver. He led the Titans in both snaps and routes against the Bengals, catching six out of seven targets for 57 yards and a touchdown. He has now drawn at least six targets in four straight games and remains a flex option. Chimere Dike caught five passes for 71 yards and a touchdown while filling in for Carnell Tate, but his role could shrink after the Week 9 bye. TE Gunnar Helm had his best game of the season with five receptions for 76 yards on nine targets, despite playing on a season-low percentage of snaps. Daniel Bellinger's increased involvement makes Helm difficult to trust outside deeper leagues.
Chase Brown led Cincinnati's backfield in snaps, routes and touches against the Titans. Brown finished with 55 rushing yards on 12 carries and caught eight out of nine targets for 46 yards, scoring 16.1 fantasy points. He also ran more than twice as many routes as Samaje Perine, highlighting his significant role in the passing game. Perine finished with just five touches for 19 yards but remains involved in the red zone. Brown's workload keeps him firmly in the RB2 conversation heading into Week 9 against a Falcons defense that ranks among the top five in fantasy points per game allowed to running backs. Perine remains as merely an insurance back.
Mike Gesicki set a season-high in snaps against the Titans following injuries to Erick All Jr. and Tanner Hudson. He ran three times as many routes as Drew Sample, and caught four out of six targets for 76 yards and a touchdown (17.6 fantasy points). Gesicki has now scored a touchdown in five straight games, but what's even more encouraging is his increased involvement on early downs and in two-TE sets. With All and Hudson out for the rest of the season, Gesicki's expanded role should continue. He's worth adding for fantasy managers needing help at tight end.
Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions

The Vikings used a three-man backfield against the Lions, with no running back playing more than 40% of snaps. Aaron Jones Sr. led the way, followed by DeeJay Dallas and Jordan Mason. Mason led the backfield with eight carries for 20 yards, while Jones had five carries for 22 yards and caught both of his targets for 18 yards. Dallas handled most of the third-down work but finished with just one touch. Jones and Mason remain difficult to trust as anything more than flex options until their roles become clearer. However, the Vikings face a Bills defense in Week 9 that has allowed the fourth-most RB fantasy points per game.
Jordan Addison has seen increased playing time in the slot over the last two games, giving him more opportunities in the Vikings passing game. Against the Lions, Addison led Minnesota receivers in snaps and caught three out of eight targets for 11.6 fantasy points. Justin Jefferson led the team with nine targets, while Jauan Jennings had just two. Addison's eight targets were a season high, which is encouraging for managers. The Vikings face the Bills and Packers over their next two games, both of whom rank among the top 10 in terms of the most WR fantasy points per game.

Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys

Tyler Allgeier took over Arizona's backfield against the Cowboys after Jeremiyah Love aggravated his ankle injury and Bam Knight suffered a concussion. Love opened the game as the primary back, with Knight taking over early-down work following his departure. Once Knight exited, Allgeier played every running back snap in the second half and overtime. He finished with 147 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, adding five receptions for 44 yards and another score for a season-high 36.1 fantasy points. Allgeier should be a priority waiver pickup with RB2 upside if Love and Knight miss Week 9 against the Seahawks. His performance could also earn him a larger role even when both return.
Arizona's receiving corps continues to battle injuries. Kendrick Bourne suffered an ankle injury, Reggie Virgil exited late, and Michael Wilson played through broken ribs. Trey McBride and Wilson dominated snaps and routes, with Wilson drawing a team-high 15 targets and finishing with 111 yards and a touchdown. McBride added seven receptions for 72 yards and a score. He's now caught at least seven passes in 10 straight games -- the third-longest streak in NFL history. Both remain must-start fantasy options as targets continue to be concentrated between them. Gardner Minshew II also replaced Jacoby Brissett and could start in Week 9.
The Cowboys rank seventh in passing attempts per game, creating plenty of opportunities for their receivers. George Pickens has dealt with shoulder and hamstring injuries over the last two weeks, leading to more frequent substitutions and increased playing time for Ryan Flournoy. When Pickens has rotated out, Flournoy has handled most of the available snaps in single-receiver sets and taken on additional work in two-WR formations. Flournoy has now drawn at least four targets and scored at least 12 fantasy points in four straight games. Monitor Pickens' practice participation this week. If he remains limited, Flournoy could be an intriguing sleeper against a vulnerable Colts defense in Week 9.

Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers

Dylan Sampson led the Browns backfield in snaps, routes run and fantasy points (12.9), largely because Cleveland was playing from behind. Quinshon Judkins still led the backfield with 13 touches, compared to only seven for Sampson. This is something fantasy managers will have to live with when rostering Judkins, whose workload is more favorable when the Browns are playing with a lead or keeping games competitive. Cleveland should have an easier time moving the ball against the Saints in Week 9, keeping Judkins in the volume-based RB2 conversation.
KC Concepcion was held to four targets and 6.7 fantasy points against the Steelers after finishing with 10 targets and a season-high 23.2 fantasy points against the Titans in Week 7. Despite leading Cleveland in routes run, Concepcion was out-targeted by both Harold Fannin Jr. (12) and Denzel Boston (11). The playing time is encouraging, but the inconsistent target volume makes Concepcion and Boston difficult to trust in fantasy lineups. Fannin has been the more reliable option, drawing at least nine targets and scoring at least 13 fantasy points in consecutive games. He remains a low-end TE1.

Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets

The Raiders made a surprising change in their backfield against the Jets, giving Mike Washington Jr. the start over Ashton Jeanty. Washington dominated early-down and goal-line work, finishing with 83 rushing yards on a career-high 25 carries after never having reached double-digit attempts in any previous game this season. Jeanty played on a season-low number of snaps, managing just 9 yards on two carries but catching three passes for 64 yards. Coach Klint Kubiak said the change wasn't disciplinary and expects both backs to remain involved. Washington should be a priority waiver pickup, while Jeanty's reduced workload makes him a riskier fantasy option.
Braelon Allen led the Jets' backfield in snaps, routes and touches (23), finishing with a season-high 23.3 fantasy points. Breece Hall missed his fifth straight game, despite practicing on a limited basis throughout the week. Allen remains a must-hold for fantasy managers regardless of whether Hall is traded or stays in New York. He's played well enough to maintain a significant role, either as the lead back or in a committee with Hall. The Jets also have one of the more favorable remaining schedules for running backs, particularly after their Week 9 matchup against the Chiefs, making Allen worth holding for the stretch run.
Adonai Mitchell had a breakout performance against the Raiders, catching seven of his nine targets for 27.2 fantasy points. Garrett Wilson led the Jets with 12 targets, finishing with 14.3. Omar Cooper Jr. wasn't targeted, despite playing more snaps than Mitchell. Cooper continues to get more opportunities in two-WR sets, although Mitchell ran more routes against the Raiders. Mitchell will be a target on waivers, but the competition for playing time makes both receivers difficult to trust consistently. Wilson remains the safest fantasy option in this receiving corps.

Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars

The Colts continued to lean on Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs against the Jaguars despite trade rumors surrounding both players. Taylor played on 79% of snaps before garbage time but finished with just 12 touches and 6.7 fantasy points. Downs led Indianapolis in routes and caught four out of five targets for 12.3 fantasy points, thanks to a receiving touchdown. His playing time increased as the Colts used more three-WR sets while playing from behind. Their fantasy outlooks could change considerably, depending on what happens before the trade deadline.
Tyler Warren returned after missing the past two games due to a groin injury and led the Colts' TE room in snaps, routes, targets (10) and fantasy points (5.8). He saw a slight dip in playing time against the Jaguars compared to the first five weeks of the season, as Will Mallory took some additional snaps in 11 personnel. Although Warren had his second-worst fantasy performance of the season, he could take on a larger role in the Colts offense if either Taylor or Downs is traded.

Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Bucky Irving rushed for 170 yards and a touchdown against the Falcons, finishing with 21 fantasy points. Irving and Kenny Gainwell split snaps evenly after Irving played on 64% of snaps over the first seven weeks. Irving remained the primary early-down back with 27 carries, while Gainwell handled all the passing-down snaps and rushed for 140 yards on 25 attempts. Poor weather conditions led Tampa Bay to run the ball on 90% of its plays, so I wouldn't expect this kind of split every week. Irving remains a must-start, having scored at least 21 fantasy points in three of his last four games.
Kyle Pitts Sr. has seen a slight dip in playing time over the last two weeks as he continues to split snaps with Charlie Woerner and Nick Muse, but his involvement in the passing game remains encouraging. He's drawn at least five targets in four straight games and scored at least 13 fantasy points in three of them.

Los Angeles Chargers at Los Angeles Rams

Kyren Williams led the Rams backfield in snaps, routes and touches (17), but Blake Corum led the way with 13.3 fantasy points. Corum finished with 11 touches and both backs scored rushing touchdowns. Corum averaged 6.6 yards per carry, compared to 3.3 for Williams. He has now scored at least 13 fantasy points in four straight games and handled at least 10 touches in three of them. The Rams continue to lean heavily on their running game, keeping both Williams and Corum fantasy relevant.
The Chargers continued their three-man backfield rotation against the Rams, with Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell splitting early-down work while Kimani Vidal handled passing situations. Vidal led the backfield in snaps and routes run, while Mitchell and Hampton saw similar playing time. Hampton finished with 27 total yards on 11 touches, while Vidal had 30 yards on 10 touches and Mitchell added 23 yards on seven touches. The Chargers offense has been a disaster, ranking last in points, touchdowns and turnovers this season. Limited opportunities and a three-man rotation make this a backfield fantasy managers should continue to avoid.

Kansas City Chiefs at Denver Broncos

Jonah Coleman took control of the Broncos backfield against the Chiefs with RJ Harvey sidelined by a knee injury. Coleman led the Broncos backfield in snaps and routes and finished with 41 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries, adding four receptions for 63 yards (20.4 fantasy points). J.K. Dobbins managed just 13 yards on seven carries. Coleman also handled goal-line work and most of the second-half snaps, making him a must-add and a solid RB2 heading into Week 9 against a Panthers defense that's allowed the second-most RB fantasy points per game.
It was frustrating for Kenneth Walker III's fantasy managers to see Emmett Johnson finish with six touches and 25.3 fantasy points, compared to Walker's 25 touches and 12.3 fantasy points. However, context is important. Johnson played on a season-low number of snaps against the Broncos, while Walker continues to dominate touches in Kansas City's backfield. Walker has handled at least 20 touches in seven out of eight games this season. Johnson remains one of the top insurance backs worth rostering, but Walker's consistent workload should keep fantasy managers confident in his outlook.

New England Patriots at Miami Dolphins

DeMario Douglas led Patriots pass catchers with 16.6 fantasy points while A.J. Brown was ruled out and Romeo Doubs remained on IR. Douglas tied for the second-most routes run despite ranking fourth in snaps among New England's pass catchers. However, he's played primarily in 11 personnel this season, which could make his weekly production inconsistent, despite the strong performance.
Ollie Gordon II remains the Dolphins' clear lead back, playing on more than 80% of offensive snaps for the second straight week. He rushed for 69 yards on 19 carries against the Patriots but failed to catch his only target, finishing with 6.9 fantasy points. Gordon handled a season-high share of early-down snaps despite Jaylen Wright being fully healthy, while Kaytron Allen didn't see any offensive snaps. Gordon has averaged nearly 18 touches over his last four games, keeping him in the RB2 conversation. However, he has caught just one pass during that stretch, making him heavily dependent on rushing production and touchdowns.

Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders

The Commanders adjusted their receiving rotation with Terry McLaurin on IR. Treylon Burks and Antonio Williams took over as Washington's primary outside receivers against the Eagles. Both played season-high shares of snaps and ran more routes than Stefon Diggs, who continued to work primarily from the slot. Burks caught three passes for 81 yards, while Williams led the team with seven targets, finishing with five receptions for 54 yards. Diggs caught three passes for 38 yards and a touchdown. Burks and Williams are worth adding in deeper leagues, while Diggs remains a TD-dependent flex option heading into a difficult Week 9 matchup against the Rams.
